proposed_fix.description: Confirm adservice's health, socket usage and memory on its pod and node, then restart or reschedule the adservice pod only after human approval if it is confirmed unhealthy.
steps: Inspect adservice pod status, readiness probe results, restarts and recent logs to identify why ~98% of inbound calls are erroring (E2, E6).
Check adservice socket counts and memory against limits (E1, E6) for leaks, exhaustion or OOM kills.
Check node-level network receive errors/drops and conntrack usage on the node hosting adservice (read-only) to rule out a node network cause (R1, R3).
If the pod is unhealthy or leaking sockets/memory, and after on-call approval, perform a rolling restart of the adservice deployment (reversible).
If errors persist and the node shows network faults, and after approval, cordon the node and reschedule the adservice pod onto another node (R1 'spread services to other nodes/pods').
Watch adservice error rate, socket and memory metrics for recovery after each change.
preconditions: Confirm the adservice error rate (E2) is still elevated now and not a past event.
Confirm that at least one other adservice replica or a safe rollout strategy exists so that a restart will not cause a full outage for callers.
Obtain on-call approval before any restart, cordon or reschedule.
Record current pod, deployment and node state for rollback.
proposed_fix.rollback: Restarts are self-recovering; if a rollout makes things worse, run `kubectl rollout undo` for the adservice deployment, and uncordon any cordoned node to restore the previous scheduling.
